yYAw79386WI.summary: A 1937 GM-produced film explaining how the automobile differential lets wheels turn at different speeds around a corner. It uses clear animations and cutaway demonstrations to build the idea from first principles.
yYAw79386WI.why: Held up as a marvel of pedagogy and the best explanation of differentials, recommended again and again.

ySuUZEjARPY.summary: Rick Hartley gives a roughly two-hour live training on proper grounding in PCB design. He explains how energy actually flows in the space between conductors, and how that governs noise, EMI, return paths and signal reflections.
ySuUZEjARPY.why: Hailed as the best video on electrical engineering and an essential, eye-opening watch for anyone designing high-speed boards.

yTkzNHF6rMs.summary: Gary Bernhardt's RubyConf 2012 talk on testing in isolation without mocking everything. It goes through behavior versus data, mutation versus immutability, and how a functional core with an imperative shell yields natural isolation and parallelism.
yTkzNHF6rMs.why: HN recommends it as the canonical presentation of 'functional core, imperative shell' and a practical answer to unit versus integration testing.

yJDv-zdhzMY.summary: The full recording of Douglas Engelbart's 1968 demonstration, which introduced the mouse, hypertext, video conferencing, word processing, and real-time collaborative editing. It runs about 100 minutes.
yJDv-zdhzMY.why: HN treats it as an essential piece of computing history that shows how many modern interface ideas were already solved in 1968.

yiw6_JakZFc.summary: Kurzgesagt examines what individuals can do about climate change, covering lesser-known carbon sources and why systemic and political change matter more than personal footprints.
yiw6_JakZFc.why: Cited in climate threads to argue that individual action is not enough and that political pressure is needed.

yCcWpzY8dIA.summary: Martin Kleppmann's GOTO Berlin 2016 talk on how collaborative editors, offline apps, and multi-datacenter databases handle concurrent updates. It covers conflict resolution approaches including operational transformation and CRDTs, with a worked look at text CRDTs.
yCcWpzY8dIA.why: Treated as the go-to approachable yet deep primer on CRDTs and collaborative editing, recommended repeatedly in threads on Automerge, local-first software and OT versus CRDT.

yFIa-Mc2KSk.summary: Greg Baugues tells his story of living with bipolar II and ADHD as a developer at a Ruby conference. He urges openness about mental illness and explains how to get help and support colleagues.
yFIa-Mc2KSk.why: Repeatedly recommended in mental health threads for its honest storytelling that resonates with developers.

y_SXXTBypIg.summary: The first video in Not Just Bikes' Strong Towns series explains the financial instability of North American cities, based on Strong Towns research. It argues that low-density suburban growth costs more to maintain than it brings in.
y_SXXTBypIg.why: HN people recommend it as the best introduction to why sprawl and car dependence are fiscally unsustainable, often pointing to the whole series.

yL_-1d9OSdk.summary: Doug Zongker's deadpan conference presentation of his famously chicken-filled paper, given at the 2007 AAAS humor session. It satirizes academic talks while showing the pitfalls of bad presentation.
yL_-1d9OSdk.why: Beloved as a humor masterpiece and often cited as required viewing on what not to do in an academic talk.

yNzQ_sLGIuA.summary: A Medlife Crisis video by cardiologist Rohin Francis on overdiagnosis and over-screening. It explains how detecting more disease does not necessarily mean saving more lives, and covers harms such as unnecessary treatment.
yNzQ_sLGIuA.why: Pointed to in threads about cancer screening, PSA tests, full-body MRIs and consumer diagnostics as an explanation of why more testing can hurt.

ybcvlxivscw.summary: Finnish YouTuber Saara improvises gibberish that mimics how various languages sound to people who do not speak them. The sentences are mostly made up, and the clip went viral.
ybcvlxivscw.why: HN points to it as a favorite example of astonishing accent mimicry and fake-language gibberish that sounds real.

ynbgMKclWWc.summary: Economist Richard Wolff's Talks at Google lecture on his book Democracy at Work. He critiques capitalism and argues for worker-run cooperatives as a path to a more democratic economy.
ynbgMKclWWc.why: HN commenters share it as an accessible case for worker cooperatives and workplace democracy as a model for a modern left.

ydqReeTV_vk.summary: A Capella Science parody of Despacito that sings through evolutionary developmental biology, explaining how a single cell becomes a body, including body-axis genes and dormant snake leg DNA. It runs about four minutes.
ydqReeTV_vk.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining four-minute introduction to evo-devo that works even for people who dislike the original song.

y71lli8MS8s.summary: Bisqwit writes a NES emulator in C++ in about 15 minutes of tool-assisted, sped-up coding, narrated with captions. It shows an accurate emulator built with a compile-time generated 6502 instruction table. Part 2 covers compiling and running it.
y71lli8MS8s.why: HN programmers admire it as a clean, clever demonstration of emulator design and as the standout of a favorite programming YouTuber.

yErKTVdETpw.summary: The full 1984 interview with Yuri Bezmenov, a former KGB operative, in which he lays out four stages of ideological subversion. It is a long interview with G. Edward Griffin.
yErKTVdETpw.why: Cited in propaganda and disinformation threads, though some commenters present it more as a prediction of current events than established analysis.

yQ16_YxLbB8.summary: The full 1997 WWDC session in which Steve Jobs, newly back at Apple, takes developer questions for about an hour. He discusses OpenDoc, Microsoft, clones, Newton, advertising and Apple's strategy.
yQ16_YxLbB8.why: HN readers recommend it as an unfiltered view of Jobs' strategic thinking and decisiveness, including the famous answer on why OpenDoc was killed.

ymaWq5yZIYM.summary: Sacha Baron Cohen's speech accepting the ADL International Leadership Award, in which he criticizes social media companies for amplifying hate and propaganda. He argues that freedom of speech is not freedom of reach.
ymaWq5yZIYM.why: Quoted heavily in moderation and free speech debates, particularly the line about freedom of speech and reach.

y7HrM-fk_Rc.summary: The first lecture in an 18-part series on digital photography from Marc Levoy's Stanford CS 178 course, recorded at Google in 2016. The series covers how digital cameras work and computational photography, with slides and assignments available on the course site.
y7HrM-fk_Rc.why: HN recommends it as a free, serious introduction to digital and computational photography from a professor who helped build the early Pixel cameras.

yS1ibDImAYU.summary: Kurzgesagt explains how accumulating space junk could trigger a collision cascade (Kessler syndrome) that makes launches too dangerous and traps humanity on Earth.
yS1ibDImAYU.why: The standard explainer HN links in satellite and debris threads for the collision-cascade risk.

y3qfeoqErtY.summary: Wendover Productions explains how overnight shipping works, covering the hub-and-spoke logistics of companies like FedEx and UPS and the use of cargo aircraft. It touches on the economics that make next-day delivery possible.
y3qfeoqErtY.why: Recommended as a clear, accessible explainer on logistics, overnight shipping and why old planes get used for cargo.

yG1OZ69H_-o.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppCon 2016 talk tries to defuse the heated debate over undefined behavior in C and C++. He explains from the compiler writer's perspective why UB exists and how it enables optimization.
yG1OZ69H_-o.why: HN points to it whenever undefined behavior comes up, as the best explanation of the reasoning behind UB, though some dispute its framing.

yQ6VOOd73MA.summary: A NOVA documentary with neuroscientist Heather Berlin exploring the subconscious and what drives our decisions. It uses sleepwalking, anesthesia, improvised rap in an MRI and game theory to probe how much of the brain's work is hidden.
yQ6VOOd73MA.why: Recommended in threads on consciousness, anesthesia and perception as a fascinating look at how much of experience the brain constructs.

ysa5OBhXz-Q.summary: George Monbiot narrates how reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone after about 70 years set off a trophic cascade. The wolves changed deer behavior, vegetation recovered, and rivers changed course.
ysa5OBhXz-Q.why: HN cites it as the go-to example of how one keystone species can reshape an entire ecosystem.

y-AXTx4PcKI.summary: The famous Alec Baldwin monologue from the film Glengarry Glen Ross, where his character Blake berates salesmen with the 'Always Be Closing' speech. It is a short, profane scene about sales pressure and motivation.
y-AXTx4PcKI.why: HN points to it as the one scene worth watching from the movie, a classic about sales and entrepreneurship.

yHXx3orN35Y.summary: 8088 MPH is a demoscene production for the original 1981 IBM PC with CGA graphics and a 4.77MHz 8088, shown with real composite output. It competed at Revision 2015 and pushes the hardware well past what it was thought capable of, breaking emulators.
yHXx3orN35Y.why: HN points to it as the standard example of what cycle-exact, hardware-level programming can achieve on ancient machines, from the colors it produces to its PC speaker audio.

yY1FSsUV-8c.summary: Andrew Sorensen's OSCON 2014 keynote in which he live-codes generative music on stage using his Impromptu environment while narrating his computational and musical choices. It imagines concert programmers as a performing art.
yY1FSsUV-8c.why: HN commenters regard it as an inspiring, all-time favorite demonstration of live coding music.

ydyztGZnbNs.summary: John Carmack live-codes a simple VR application at Oculus Connect 2 using a Racket-based environment for rapid development and deployment on Gear VR.
ydyztGZnbNs.why: Cited for watching Carmack code fluently and for the fast iteration cycle of Racket-based VR scripting.

ytpRnRke6I0.summary: A Technology Connections update video in which Alec Watson tests an Onyx Boox Max e-ink Android tablet used as an external display and shares channel news. It describes his experience with large-format e-ink.
ytpRnRke6I0.why: HN recommends it as a thorough real-world account of using an e-ink tablet as a computer monitor.

yvDCzhbjYWs.summary: Peter Norvig's UBC distinguished lecture on how massive amounts of simple data, such as for language modeling, can yield understanding that hand-built models could not.
yvDCzhbjYWs.why: Recommended as a favorite tech talk showing how huge data availability changes how problems are approached.

y-uuk4Pr2i8.summary: A very short animation of a kinesin motor protein walking along a microtubule inside a cell, carrying cargo.
y-uuk4Pr2i8.why: Shared as a vivid illustration of molecular machines at work inside cells.

yCsgoLc_fzI.summary: Veritasium recounts a $10,000 bet with a UCLA physics professor over whether a vehicle can travel downwind faster than the wind. He presents the professor's reasoning and demonstrations, including one without aerodynamics.
yCsgoLc_fzI.why: Linked as clear demonstrations that make the counterintuitive faster-than-wind result click.

yXbJe-rUNP8.summary: A five-hour documentary history of the Super Mario 64 A button challenge, which aims to beat the game with as few A presses as possible. It covers the bugs and exploits discovered over the years.
yXbJe-rUNP8.why: Recommended as a deep-dive rabbit hole showing extraordinary knowledge of game internals.

yY9GAyJtuJ0.summary: CodeParade's short devlog on how spherical geometry looks in 2D and 3D and why it feels so unusual, part of the Hyperbolica series on a non-Euclidean game.
yY9GAyJtuJ0.why: Recommended among the nice visual explorations and tech demos of non-Euclidean geometry for games.

yvFKh_3evC8.summary: Part one of a 1996 BBC Modern Times documentary on the training to become a London black cab driver. It follows candidates learning the Knowledge and facing stressful repeated exams with Public Carriage Office examiners.
yvFKh_3evC8.why: HN commenters recommend it whenever London cabbies and the Knowledge come up, as an interesting if slightly dated look at the process.

yy8jQgmhbAU.summary: A CppCon 2018 talk arguing that OOP has failed to deliver on reuse and performance, and presenting data-oriented design for C++ with practical worked examples from real systems.
yy8jQgmhbAU.why: HN cites it as a concrete, worked example of data-oriented design and as an alternative to OOP in performance-sensitive code.

y5UT04p5f7U.summary: CGP Grey's short animated argument for abolishing the US penny, covering its cost and history.
y5UT04p5f7U.why: Pointed to as the canonical concise case against pennies whenever coin abolition comes up.

yYTSdlOdkn0.summary: James Hoffmann explains how decaf coffee is made, how the decaffeination processes differ, and why decaf is roasted and stales differently. He also discusses decaf quality and health questions.
yYTSdlOdkn0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a well-researched overview of decaf processes and quality, and cite it for the claim that decaf stales faster.

yqMjMPlXzdA.summary: A 45-minute Flex Your Rights documentary on how to deal with police in three situations: traffic stops, encounters at home, and on the street. It presents practical advice on asserting constitutional rights and refusing searches.
yqMjMPlXzdA.why: Recommended as a practical guide to knowing your rights during police encounters, alongside the well-known advice to not talk to the cops.

ywWBy6J5gz8.summary: Hungarian folk dancers from Sapientia University act out the quicksort algorithm step by step, with music. It is part of the AlgoRythmics series of sorting algorithms performed as dance.
ywWBy6J5gz8.why: HN recommends it as a memorable and fun way to visualize how sorting algorithms work.

y2Wmz15aXk0.summary: A 10-minute clip from a Jonathan Blow Twitch stream in which he argues that game engines do not really need separate scripting languages. He questions the value of embedded interpreters when the main language can do the job.
y2Wmz15aXk0.why: Cited in threads about Lua, embedded scripting, and game engines as a concise argument that scripting languages are redundant.

y4GB_NDU43Q.summary: Tom Scott performs a fictional story at GeekyConf about the day Google accidentally stops checking passwords, letting anyone into any account. It works as a parable about how a single point of failure in login can unravel everything built on it.
y4GB_NDU43Q.why: HN commenters cite it as the canonical thought experiment whenever authentication failures, account compromises or Google outages come up.

y4sOfO8Ei1g.summary: A kinetic typography animation for Jonathan Coulton's song 'Shop Vac', made by Jarrett Heather with Illustrator, After Effects and other tools over 500-1000 hours.
y4sOfO8Ei1g.why: Praised as a standout example of kinetic typography that holds attention, and known as the earlier work that led to the animator's Weird Al 'Word Crimes' video.

yCd3CzGSte8.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Chris Lattner, creator of LLVM, Clang and Swift, about compilers, Swift for TensorFlow, TPUs and ML accelerators. The talk covers how hardware and software meet to produce efficient code.
yCd3CzGSte8.why: HN commenters point to it as an interesting conversation with the creator of Swift and LLVM, especially for compilers and ML compilation.

yCm9Ng0bbEQ.summary: Steven Pinker's TED talk presents data on homicide, war, poverty and pollution to argue that the world has improved over the past decades. He frames progress as problem-solving, not inevitability.
yCm9Ng0bbEQ.why: Cited as a data-backed counter to doom and pessimism about the state of the world.

yF2KgQGmUic.summary: Matt Ahrens presents the FreeBSD Foundation sponsored RAID-Z Expansion project for ZFS at the June 2021 FreeBSD Developer Summit. It explains how a RAID-Z vdev can be grown by adding disks on the fly.
yF2KgQGmUic.why: HN points to it as the video explanation of how RAID-Z expansion works without block pointer rewrite.

yReDbeY7ZMU.summary: First part of a six-part recording of the 1973 Lighthill debate on AI, where Sir James Lighthill's critical report on AI research was contested by figures including McCarthy and Michie.
yReDbeY7ZMU.why: Recommended as a historical look at the AI winter debate and a demolition of the expert systems hype.

yY96hTb8WgI.summary: Vox's Joe Posner, with help from 99% Invisible, explains why bad doors are everywhere. It covers Don Norman's long-running complaint about doors and the idea that good design should not need instructions.
yY96hTb8WgI.why: HN uses it as the short, canonical explainer of Norman doors and affordances, linked in design and UX discussions.

yaonVYOTSsk.summary: The Centre for Computing History reunites Chris Curry, Steve Furber and Hermann Hauser to rewatch the BBC drama Micro Men on its tenth anniversary. They reminisce about Acorn and the early British home computer era.
yaonVYOTSsk.why: Recommended as a companion to Micro Men, with the real Acorn people commenting on how events actually happened.

yhGjCzxJV3E.summary: A GDC 2015 talk by Arc System Works technical artist Junya Motomura on how Guilty Gear Xrd rebuilt a classic 2D fighter in full 3D while keeping a hand-drawn look. It covers the art and programming R&D and the stylistic decisions behind it.
yhGjCzxJV3E.why: HN points to it as the definitive example of making 3D rendering look like 2D animation through cel shading, outlines, and framerate tricks.

yhO6jfHPFQU.summary: Primer uses simulations to compare voting systems such as first-past-the-post, approval, ranked choice and others. It shows how each system behaves and can be manipulated, with links to further voting theory resources.
yhO6jfHPFQU.why: HN commenters link it to explain why plurality voting produces two-party systems and how ranked-choice voting suffers spoiler effects.

ypn3Fe_PLts.summary: Soup Emporium's deep dive argues that Yellowstone is not a ticking timebomb. It goes through uplift and subsidence, earthquakes and what the caldera really is, to rebut supervolcano doom claims.
ypn3Fe_PLts.why: Linked whenever Yellowstone or caldera unrest comes up, as the debunking of civilization-ending eruption fears.

ytyjgIyegDI.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder explains superdeterminism as an interpretation of quantum mechanics, addressing common objections and misconceptions, including the worry that it kills free will or science. She ties it to Bell's theorem and hidden variables.
ytyjgIyegDI.why: HN commenters point to it as a clear explanation of Bell's theorem and superdeterminism, though some criticize it as knocking down strawmen.

yvBR71D0nAQ.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2018 session on how DynamoDB was built as a hyper-scale NoSQL database. It discloses underpinnings of the service and how it is run for over 100,000 customers.
yvBR71D0nAQ.why: HN points to it as an authoritative look at DynamoDB internals and as evidence it is a complex distributed system.

yvhv7bgmz64.summary: Videogamedunkey's satirical guide to the fragmented streaming service landscape, ending in a joke about how to watch King Kong.
yvhv7bgmz64.why: Recommended as a funny but surprisingly accurate illustration of streaming fragmentation driving piracy.

yFVXsjVdvmY.summary: Mathematician Hannah Fry's TED talk on patterns in dating and mate-seeking, including optimal stopping and three math-backed tips for finding a partner.
yFVXsjVdvmY.why: Mentioned whenever the optimal stopping or secretary problem comes up in relation to choosing a partner.

yMjPqr1s-cg.summary: Ted Nelson's short eulogy for Douglas Engelbart, delivered at the Computer History Museum in 2013, reflecting on his friend and Engelbart's ideas.
yMjPqr1s-cg.why: Recommended as a moving tribute that laments how little of Engelbart's vision caught on.

ycPr5-27vSI.summary: A roughly 2.5-hour Joe Rogan conversation with Elon Musk covering AI, simulation theory, climate, his companies and his mindset.
ycPr5-27vSI.why: Recommended as a long, wide-ranging look into Musk's thinking, especially on AI and the future of humanity.

yftBiNu0ZNU.summary: Chubbyemu presents a case study of a man who followed AI health advice, replaced salt with sodium bromide and developed bromism with severe neurological effects. It is told as a dramatized medical case by a doctor.
yftBiNu0ZNU.why: Used in AI threads as a cautionary example of harm from LLM self-diagnosis, though some commenters cite it as part of broader criticism of AI.

ygB4EZ7ggig.summary: A 60 Minutes segment in which Navy pilots Dave Fravor and Alex Dietrich recount their 2004 encounter with the 'tic tac' UAP during training with the USS Nimitz group.
ygB4EZ7ggig.why: Cited in UFO threads as a short, first-hand pilot account worth hearing, even without papers or data.

y57wwucbXR8.summary: Andrej Karpathy's Databricks talk on Software 2.0, the shift from human-written code to code produced by neural network training. It covers how developer work moves toward curating datasets, the advantages and challenges, and opportunities for new tooling.
y57wwucbXR8.why: HN uses it as the primary source for the 'Software 2.0' idea and recommends it as a quick talk on the next software stack.

y7h4OtFDnYE.summary: A short clip from the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine in which Richard Feynman explains how a train stays on the track. He covers the geometry of tapered wheels that steer the train back toward the center of the rails.
y7h4OtFDnYE.why: HN people link it as Feynman's charming and clear explanation of why train wheels are tapered, whenever trains, bicycles or steering come up.

yRdzIs4FJJg.summary: FortNine looks at why Tesla Autopilot has rear-ended motorcyclists, speculating that the vision system misreads motorcycle taillights as a distant car. It argues that radar and other sensors would help.
yRdzIs4FJJg.why: Cited in threads on motorcycle safety, Tesla's sensor choices and autonomous vehicles as a well-made explanation of the failure mode.

yS_c2qqA-6Y.summary: Adam Curtis's 2016 BBC documentary argues that since the 1970s governments, financiers and technologists have retreated into a simplified fake world. It ranges from Syria and Libya to the road to Trump.
yS_c2qqA-6Y.why: Mentioned as a recommended Curtis film and referenced in discussions of AI, Eliza and manufactured realities.

yT9bit2-1pg.summary: Wendover Productions explains counterintuitive riot control techniques based on research, showing that effective tactics tend to avoid violence.
yT9bit2-1pg.why: Cited for its research-based principles of riot control, and as an analogy for managing other crowd dynamics like bubbles.

yVCOAFKjaoY.summary: A short clip from the NBC sitcom Community in which a character delivers a monologue about how LEGO changed over the years. It is the source of a widely quoted passage about the toy.
yVCOAFKjaoY.why: HN commenters link it as the origin of a LEGO quote and as a delightful monologue about how the toy has changed.

yW2LpFkVfYk.summary: A Fox News segment in which Ami Horowitz interviews people at UC Berkeley and in Harlem about whether voter ID laws are racist.
yW2LpFkVfYk.why: Cited in voting-related threads as a favorite example of street interviews on voter ID, though it is a partisan satirical piece.

yYUuWWnfRsk.summary: Boston Dynamics introduces Stretch, a prototype robot that moves boxes in warehouses and distribution centers. Its mobile base lets it unload trucks, build pallets and assemble orders.
yYUuWWnfRsk.why: HN links it as the official demo showing what Stretch actually does, though some commenters point out its limits, such as picking boxes from one side.

yg-UqIIvang.summary: A short scene from the British sitcom Yes Prime Minister in which officials describe 'salami tactics' for invading a country slice by slice. Each small step is too minor to justify a major response.
yg-UqIIvang.why: HN uses it as shorthand for incremental aggression and escalation, in threads on geopolitics, trade and creeping encroachment.

ymoiWv9BF7Q.summary: Geekerwan's Chinese-language review of Intel's Lunar Lake lightweight laptop chip, covering performance, perf-per-watt curves and battery life benchmarks. It tests whether x86 can compete on efficiency.
ymoiWv9BF7Q.why: HN uses it as a benchmark source in debates over whether x86 can match Apple Silicon efficiency, particularly the Lunar Lake vs M3 comparison.

yts2F44RqFw.summary: An Innuendo Studios Alt-Right Playbook episode about a rhetorical tactic of dismissing partial fixes to problems. It frames this as a style of argument that treats flaws as unfixable facts of life.
yts2F44RqFw.why: Referenced to describe an argument style that rejects incremental improvements, and in discussions of differing liberal and conservative views of society.

yw--NLjZBNk.summary: Chef Chris Young shows a simplified triple-cooked method for making crisp frozen fries in an air fryer, based on Heston Blumenthal's technique.
yw--NLjZBNk.why: Cited as proof that frozen fries can be excellent with the right cooking method.

yx7-yvXf6f8.summary: A short Boeing piece on the retirement of the voice behind the F/A-18 Super Hornet cockpit warning system, nicknamed Bitchin' Betty. It touches on why the stern voice alerts are used.
yx7-yvXf6f8.why: Cited as an example of effective alarm and voice-alert design and in discussions of reactions to female voices.

y0vlD7r-kTc.summary: A 35C3 talk by Privacy International researchers who captured and decrypted traffic between Android apps and Facebook servers. They show many apps send Facebook device and usage data immediately on launch, even for users without Facebook accounts.
y0vlD7r-kTc.why: HN cites it as the source for how Facebook's SDK tracks Android users by default.

y2F0wjoKEhg.summary: Linus Tech Tips backs up their petabyte server to Google's unlimited G Suite Drive plan and runs into the daily upload cap. It shows how far the 'unlimited' offer can be pushed.
y2F0wjoKEhg.why: Cited as an example of data hoarders testing Google's unlimited storage and of Google rate limiting heavy use.

y39D4529FM4.summary: A short 2001 Tom's Hardware clip that runs Quake 3 on several popular CPU and motherboard combinations of the era, then removes the CPU cooler to see which chips survive. It shows how different processors handle losing their heatsink or fan.
y39D4529FM4.why: HN commenters cite it as the famous demonstration of what happens to CPUs without thermal protection, especially the Athlon burning out.

y3InF19dzlM.summary: IIHS frontal crash test footage showing what happens to an unbelted rear-seat passenger. It illustrates that buckling up in the back matters for the passenger and for front occupants.
y3InF19dzlM.why: Used as a visual example in seat belt and personal-freedom debates, showing an unbelted rear passenger becoming a projectile.

y3RIHnK0_NE.summary: A Corridor Digital parody of a Boston Dynamics promo, showing a CGI military robot trained for combat that goes rogue and refuses to kill a robotic dog.
y3RIHnK0_NE.why: Used as a Skynet joke and cited as a parody that fooled some viewers into thinking it was real.

y8OnoxKotPQ.summary: A short KRAZAM comedy sketch in which engineers explain an absurdly tangled microservices architecture to a manager. It parodies how backend complexity gets justified with jargon.
y8OnoxKotPQ.why: Posted as a joke or shorthand whenever a thread touches microservices, architecture sprawl, naming, or talking to management.

yDp3cB5fHXQ.summary: A nearly four-hour video essay by hbomberguy on plagiarism on YouTube, centered on specific creators who copied other people's work. It examines what plagiarism is and how it went unaddressed.
yDp3cB5fHXQ.why: Used as a reference example of blatant plagiarism, including in debates about AI training and academic plagiarism.

yITr127KZtQ.summary: Cities: Skylines experiment measuring traffic flow across 30 different four-way junction designs, comparing vanilla traffic AI with the TMPE mod.
yITr127KZtQ.why: Cited as an example of game-based traffic simulation and intersection design comparison.

yO9VRtrTJwc.summary: A South Park clip in which Butters' dad takes a job at an Amazon fulfillment center to make ends meet. It satirizes warehouse work conditions.
yO9VRtrTJwc.why: HN uses it as a joking reference when threads discuss Amazon warehouse working conditions and surveillance.

yS7Jb58hcsc.summary: A four-minute clip of Milton Friedman, from a 1978 address, discussing property taxes and land value taxation. He says property tax is the least bad tax and explains why it is so unpopular.
yS7Jb58hcsc.why: HN cites it in tax and housing threads as a libertarian economist endorsing property or land taxes.

yVwAodrjZMY.summary: Edward Snowden appears by telepresence robot at TED2014 to discuss surveillance, privacy rights, and Internet freedom, interviewed by Chris Anderson with Tim Berners-Lee.
yVwAodrjZMY.why: Mostly referenced in debates about Snowden and surveillance rather than recommended; some commenters criticize his statements.

yaXma6K9mzo.summary: Matt Damon appears on Hot Ones, eating progressively spicier wings while discussing his film career and promoting Stillwater. He also explains how the decline of the DVD market changed which movies get made.
yaXma6K9mzo.why: Cited as the source for Damon's explanation that the DVD market's collapse killed mid-budget movies, in threads on Hollywood economics.

ybSzoLCCX-Y.summary: A four-minute clip from Dr. Strangelove in which the President and General Turgidson argue over the 'mineshaft gap' after a nuclear war. Peter Sellers and George C. Scott play it as Cold War satire.
ybSzoLCCX-Y.why: HN commenters post it as a punchline whenever a thread turns to some 'gap' or to surviving nuclear catastrophe.

ybrQvs4x0Ps.summary: Tony Hoare's InfoQ talk in which he describes introducing null references in ALGOL W in 1965 and calls it his billion-dollar mistake. He discusses language designer responsibility and run-time checks.
ybrQvs4x0Ps.why: The standard citation whenever null safety and language design come up.

yfl6Lu3xQW0.summary: The classic Fawlty Towers scene in which Basil Fawlty tries not to mention the war while serving German guests, ending in goose-stepping and mocking. It is a two-minute BBC comedy clip with John Cleese.
yfl6Lu3xQW0.why: HN mentions it mainly as a joke reference or as an example of humor that many Germans reportedly find funny.

yhuMLpdnOjY.summary: Tom Lehrer performs his satirical song about poisoning pigeons in the park, in a rare 1967 Norwegian broadcast recording.
yhuMLpdnOjY.why: Posted as a humorous reference in threads about pigeons or Lehrer.

yi8_9WGk3Ok.summary: Louis Rossmann recounts calling NYC's Department of Consumer Affairs after his repair business was fined, only to find the agency staff could not explain what the law required. The call starts around 3:14.
yi8_9WGk3Ok.why: HN cites it as a concrete example of bureaucrats not knowing the rules they enforce on small businesses.

yjfrJzdx7DA.summary: An Onion News Network satirical segment about a memorial dedicated to the future victims of a dam that officials know will fail. It is a dark joke about known infrastructure risk and inaction.
